fieldMarks: Male: uniformly gray and dark, with reddish bare neck patches ringed in white feathers visible during courtship.
Over most of the range, dark tail with a broad gray tip.
behavior: Males give a series of deep hoots in the breeding season, increasing in tempo and volume.
Slow-moving and inconspicuous but often surprisingly tame.
Feeds on the ground in summer and in trees in winter, especially in deep snow.
Unusual uphill altitudinal migration: moves up into dense conifer forest in autumn, up to about 30 miles.
habitat: Deciduous and mixed mountain forest in summer, especially where forest meets open country such as sagebrush flats; higher-elevation conifer forest in winter.
range: Western North America: Rocky Mountains and interior West from Alaska, Yukon and western Canada south to the US Southwest.

lookalikes.name: Sooty grouse
lookalikes.howToTell: Recently split from the dusky grouse; the two were formerly combined as 'blue grouse'.
